decision: Retain the compiler changes and their validated optional optimized host, but do not promote a new performance baseline. The laptop pilot fails its release compilation comparison; a bounded diagnostic does not reproduce it. Both observations remain recorded, with release timing unresolved.

hardware.policy: Existing powersave governor retained; CPU 1, one emitter, nice 10. No packages installed, settings changed or other processes stopped.

scope: Seven compilation workloads, seven paired samples and a discarded warmup; four runtime kernels in both modes against C -O2. About 60 seconds for the initial laptop pilot. One short release-only diagnostic follows; no repeated acceptance campaign.
configuration: Fresh maintained O3 PGO/LTO host with omitted frame pointers, from independently C-bootstrapped native build 1792439437291931994. Native compiler is based on revision 490ff63a; control host is based on 259e2c5c.
interpretation: The 44,005-line default workload takes 217.06 ms wall / 214.86 ms CPU: about 203k / 205k root lines per second. This is below 250k. Imported-library compilation is included in the elapsed time but imported lines are excluded from the numerator. These are fresh compiler processes with warm filesystem caches, not incremental builds.
Initial compile comparisons: six pass, release regression (paired median ratio 1.0293, interval 1.0235–1.0561). Absolute medians vary more because the machine changes speed during the sequence.

The follow-up changes the experiment: four rotating variants, phase reporting, and instruction counts. Both native and optimized host comparisons pass; neither justifies erasing the original failure. Frequency, thermal state, and ordering remain possible confounders, not proven causes.
Desktop instruction counts decrease 0.23% default, 0.54% release, and 0.96% fixed compiler rebuild. Laptop release counters independently decrease for both native and optimized builds.

Laptop C comparisons show records ahead of C, text 1.06x default / 1.15x release, managed parameters 2.71x / 1.54x, and branch dispatch 1.20x / 1.18x. This small selection does not establish C-equivalent performance generally.
All 28 local generated-artifact comparisons retain equivalent code with fresh checksums. Laptop timing variation on unchanged code is not evidence of a new generated-code regression.
Fixed reference ea1cba0e and accepted whole-stage cd07ea34 remain unchanged. This laptop pilot is supplemental evidence, not the full fixed-reference acceptance gate.

desktop_runtime_proof.scope: Fresh artifact and checksum checks for all twelve existing kernels; seven paired timing samples only for workloads whose code changed.

artifact_proof.sample_order: Rotating positions and direction; identical artifacts share explicitly labeled samples when enabled.

limits: Native 64-bit host. Warm filesystem caches; one build per binary.
C graph uses flat edges and a handwritten map; Dewy uses per-node arrays and an insertion-ordered map.
String equality uses separately allocated payloads; C uses pointer/length pairs and libc memcmp, Dewy uses runtime strings.
Kernel times exclude input generation; wall times include the complete process.
Thread CPU timing excludes descheduling, but CPU frequency and cache contention still matter.
